# CompBioBench v1: A benchmark of 100 diverse, verifiable questions for agents for computational biology

We introduce CompBioBench v1, a benchmark of 100 diverse tasks for evaluating agentic systems in computational biology. Unlike mathematics and programming, which more readily admit systematic verification, biological data are inherently noisy and open to interpretation. To enable objective evaluation without reducing tasks to prescriptive checklists, we propose a new benchmark-construction strategy based on synthetic/augmented data and metadata scrambling/scrubbing of real datasets to create challenging problems with a single ground-truth answer that require multi-step reasoning, tool use, bespoke code, and interaction with real-world external resources. /bin/bash -lc "Rscript -e '
library(Seurat)
full<-readRDS(\"Mouse_SS_Fibro.RDS\")
q<-readRDS(\"tissue.fibroblast.q1.rds\")
cat(\"loaded\\n\")
targets<-c(\"Cell_11249_MCI\",\"Cell_10369_WXV\")
qc<-GetAssayData(full,slot=\"counts\")
# ensure same genes and order
cat(\"genes identical\", identical(rownames(q), rownames(qc)), \"query dim\", dim(q), \"full dim\", dim(qc),\"\\n\")
for(cc in targets){
  v<-q[,cc]
  s<-sum(v); nz<-sum(v>0)
  cat(\"\\nTarget\",cc,\"sum\",s,\"nz\",nz,\"\\n\")
  # candidate by colSums may be memory; compute full sums once
}
fs<-Matrix::colSums(qc)
cat(\"full sums computed\\n\")
for(cc in targets){
  v<-q[,cc]; s<-sum(v)
  idx<-which(fs==s)
  cat(cc,\"candidates total\",length(idx),\"\\n\")
  if(length(idx)>0 && length(idx)<=5000){
    # compare sparse vector equality for candidates
    found<-which(vapply(idx, function(j) isTRUE(all.equal(v, qc[,j], check.attributes=FALSE)), logical(1)))
    cat(\"exact matches\",length(found),\"\\n\")
    if(length(found)>0) print(data.frame(idx=idx[found], cell=colnames(qc)[idx[found]], tissue=full"'$Tissue[idx[found]], clust=full$ClustName[idx[found]]))
  } else if(length(idx)>5000){cat("too many candidates; refining by nz'"\\n\")}
}
'"
